4. The defendant opposite party Nos. 1-3 contested the matter of temporary injunction by submitting written objection on 9-5-1991 denying generally the case of plaintiff petitioners and stating, inter alla, that the suit is not properly called and stamped, that the suit property is not properly described in the schedule of the plaint and that Kalimuddin exchanged his properties with land of Nagendra Nath Biswas and others and came to the country with Miasuddin. and Raisuddin. Miasuddin did not acquire any more right by the Power of Attorney than validating the exchange by necessary documentation. The exchange case is pending but Kalimuddin died in 1975 leaving Miasuddin and Raisuddn to inherit him. Raisuddin used to live in village Aichagate of Khulna Sadar and was a voter in 1976. Then he lived in village Bhanikara of Avoynagar P. S. under district Jessore and sold out 2.59 and odd acres of land on 13-8-84 and 2.77 and odd acres of land at the same time to the defendants who, thereafter engaged bargadars for taking possession of the lands purchased by them out of the suit land. The bargadars took possession of the lands and the plaintiffs filed a criminal case. Miasuddin filed another criminal case being G. R. Case No. 855 of 1986 in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Khulna. The defendants were acquitted on trial on 30-8-88. The defendants purchased. 2050 acre of land of plot No. 18 of Chargram Mouza from Debendra and Khagendra and built their dwelling house there in. There was a pre-emotion case filed Sayera Khatoon on the strength of co-sharer ship and she won the case. Miscellaneous Case under Section 150 of the State acquisition and tenancy Act for reviewing the mutation of plaintiffs name was filed by the defendants which was allowed. Plaintiffs have no title in the suit land. The plaintiffs filed the criminal case being C. R. Case No. 5 of 1990 against the relatives of the defendant opposite parties. There was a salish by 3 advocates of Bagerhat District Bar Association on 2-1-90 and the salish held that Miasuddin along can not succeed his father Kalimuddin in respect of the exchange property. 

 7. Mr. K. S. Zaman the learned  Advocate appearing for the petitioners has submitted that the learned Judge of the Court of appeal below reversed the order of injunction granted by the court of trial on the solitary ground that the land S. A. Khatian No. 378 is not clearly described in the schedule of the plaint and in the petition for temporary injunction and the learned Judge failed to observe that the land of Plot No. 200, 201 measuring 1.22 acres entitle constitute a single block of land and the plaintiffs clearly stated that they possess 60 acre out of the 2 plots from the eastern side even though they failed to mention by inadvertence of the learned Advocate as to what quantum of land of each plot is possessed by them. 

 8. Mr. Zaman has further submitted that the learned Judge should have found that it was no defect at all, but a mere irregular forensic parlance. And, while the learned Judge held that it was a defect, he should have been pleased to either direct the plaintiffs-petitioners to amend or grant injunction for the rest of the suit land excluding the said 2 plots to secure the ends of justice. Mr. Zaman has further submitted that the court of Appeal below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice failing to observe that plot No. 200 and 201 measuring. 66 and 56 acres respectively of Khatian 378 constitute one block of land and it has been clearly stated in the schedule of the plaint and in the  petition for temporary injunction. Mr. Zaman  has further submitted that the learned court of appeal below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by failing to direct the plaintiff petitioners to amend description of the suit land or, in the alternative, grant prayer for temporary injunction excluding Khatian No. 378 (of the said plots being plot Nos. 200. 201) to secure the ends of justice. Mr. Zaman further submitted that the learned Judge of the court below committed an error of law resulting in an the decision occasioning failure of his tice by misreading the pleadings of the petitioners and by not applying judicial mind to the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 14. Mr. Sk. Atiar Rahman in support of his contention has referred to 42 DLR (HCD) P-434 and has submitted that the failure of the plaintiffs to give specification of the suit lands and plaintiffs having failed to comply with the mandatory requirement of law in giving descriptions sufficient to identify the suit land they are not entitled to get any relief even if they succeed in proving their title. Mr. Sk. Attar Rahman by filling an affidavit in the form of an application have filed document on behalf of the opposite parties and have stated that the defendants have been inducted into the possession on getting the same and they have their dwelling house in the suit properly. Mr. Atiar Rahman further submitted that the plain-tiffs exchange case is still pending and until and unless the exchange deed is validated no title is accrued to the plaintiff and in the facts and circumstances of the case the rule obtained by the petitioners is liable to be discharged. Mr. Sk. Attar Rahman has also filed a supplementary affidavit dated 13-12-95 and has submit-ted that the exchange deed has been made after 1956 and therefore, in accordance with law any circular, the same has got no value.
